content.text:
**Recommend Cloudflare Workers with Slack HTTP ingress for Clanker’s trusted gateway. Reuse Hermes inside isolated workers through its existing runs API.** This fits the chosen architecture, but it does **not** mean the pinned Slack adapter runs unchanged on Workers.

I inspected the actual pinned checkout: Hermes **0.21.5**, commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`. Its tracked files are clean. Findings below are source-verified; hosted behavior remains untested.

### What can be reused

| Component | Verified finding | Practical reuse |
|---|---|---|
| Slack transport | `SlackAdapter.connect()` explicitly starts Bolt `AsyncSocketModeHandler`; app token is mandatory. | Unchanged reuse requires a normal Python process. |
| Event handling | Existing handlers cover messages, mentions, files, reactions, slash commands, thread context and interactive controls. | Reuse in a Python backend, or selectively port the behavior needed by Clanker. |
| Replies | Adapter already supports threaded replies, formatting, status updates, streaming and files. | Valuable backend reuse; unavailable directly to TypeScript Workers. |
| Remote execution | Stock proxy mode posts to `/v1/chat/completions`, streams text and sends a session ID. | Useful split-runtime demonstration, insufficient for Clanker’s durable task/control contract. |
| Asynchronous runs | `/v1/runs` supplies admission, status, events, approval, steering and stop endpoints, plus durable idempotency. | Best existing integration surface for isolated Hermes workers. |

Relevant pinned sources: [Slack transport and listeners](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:1601), [proxy request construction](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/gateway/run_turn.py:2744), [runs endpoints](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py:186).

### Three viable approaches

| Approach | Benefit | Remaining work | Judgment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Workers HTTP gateway → isolated Hermes runs API** | Prompt ingress independent of worker availability; trusted controls stay outside agent execution. | Slack normalization, delivery, authorization, durable task records and scheduling. | **Recommended architecture.** |
| **Workers HTTP ingress → Python Slack adapter backend** | Preserves most existing Slack behavior. | Add an HTTP lifecycle to the adapter, durable queued dispatch and remote execution controls. | Reasonable if extensive Slack feature parity is required immediately. |
| **Container-hosted stock Socket Mode gateway** | Least transport modification. | Always-running connection, durable persistence, scheduling and owner checks still required. | Fastest baseline, less suitable as the final gateway. |

Slack Bolt officially supports HTTP through its ASGI adapters, so the second approach has a supported **Slack SDK seam**. However, pinned Hermes has no HTTP transport switch: wiring it requires a targeted adapter extension, not configuration alone. [Bolt ASGI documentation](https://tools.slack.dev/bolt-python/api-docs/slack_bolt/adapter/asgi/index.html).

Python Workers is now supported, but its runtime has nonfunctional threading/multiprocessing and ephemeral filesystem storage. The actual Hermes gateway uses threads, executors, subprocesses and local state. **Treat unchanged Hermes-on-Workers as incompatible with the inspected execution model; no portability test was performed.** [Cloudflare runtime documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/python/stdlib/).

### Exact custom work for the recommended approach

1. **Authenticated ingress:** verify Slack HMAC against the raw body, validate timestamp freshness, handle URL verification, and parse Events API JSON plus form-encoded slash commands/interactions. Derive installation, workspace, sender and audience from authenticated payloads. [Slack verification](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/verifying-requests-from-slack/).

2. **Durable acceptance:** record acceptance before returning success; use an outbox or equivalent recoverable dispatch transition. Slack expects acknowledgement within three seconds and retries failed deliveries. Do not wait for a worker to start. [Events API](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/).

3. **Routing and dispatch:** assign a server-controlled context and worker, invoke `/v1/runs` with stable idempotency/session identifiers, and persist the run association. Cloudflare Queues supports external HTTP consumers and at-least-once delivery, so duplicates and conversation serialization need explicit handling. Keep queue credentials in trusted dispatch infrastructure. [Pull consumers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/), [delivery guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/).

4. **Replies and controls:** retain Slack tokens in the trusted gateway, consume worker results, enforce destination/audience policy, and deliver via Slack APIs. Persist approval records binding owner, task, exact action, expiry and request ID. Acknowledge interactions promptly; delayed results use standard message delivery when needed. [Slack interactions](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/).

5. **Recovery:** reconcile accepted tasks, interrupted runs and uncertain deliveries. Hermes’s durable run records detect interrupted execution; they do not restore an in-flight browser action or establish safe automatic replay.

### Authorization caveats remain

The existing [Slack audit](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/audit-slack-notes.md) establishes that stock approval buttons check bot admission rather than resource ownership, broad sender routes can select private profiles in shared channels, and unmatched routes fall back.

The runs API improves the integration surface: it checks run ownership by authenticated API scope and supports exact approval request IDs. **That scope is not automatically the Slack human owner.** Clanker must make that binding itself. Likewise, profiles remain insufficient isolation for agent-accessible resources.

Stock Slack deduplication is an in-memory TTL cache, not durable acceptance: [implementation](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/gateway/platforms/helpers.py:20). It also merges duplicate message/mention notifications by workspace and event timestamp; HTTP ingress needs equivalent semantic deduplication alongside envelope-ID deduplication.

### Supported bridge alternative

Pinned Hermes includes an **experimental RelayAdapter** with normalized inbound events, outbound operations and connector-owned Slack credentials. It is conceptually close to this architecture.

However, its contract relies on a separate `NousResearch/gateway-gateway` connector and WebSocket transport. The referenced repository returned HTTP 404 during research; public availability and Slack support could not be established. Porting its connector/bus to Workers would also require work. **Do not make v1 depend on it without proving availability and behavior.** [Pinned contract](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/developer-guide/relay-connector-contract.md:1).

### Cost and decision

Workers Free currently includes **100,000 requests/day**. Queues Free includes **10,000 operations/day**, with **24-hour retention**; normal delivery uses roughly three operations per small message. Workers Paid starts at **$5/month**, with queue/storage overages separate. These figures cover the gateway, not browser workers or inference. [Workers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/), [Queues pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/platform/pricing/).

Cloudflare Containers requires the paid plan and adds running memory, CPU, disk, egress and Durable Object costs. A persistent Socket Mode gateway loses much of the scale-to-zero benefit, and container disk requires an explicit persistence strategy. [Container pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), [container lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/concepts/architecture/).

**Decision needed:** whether Clanker requires broad Hermes Slack feature parity immediately. For DMs, mentions, threaded replies, progress and owner-bound controls, choose the Workers gateway plus runs API. For extensive native slash commands, streaming, file handling and assistant surfaces immediately, retain a Python adapter backend behind Workers.

Research completed read-only: no files, credentials, Slack settings, deployments, VMs or board content were changed.
I’ll draft the gateway PRD around one shared gateway and dynamic dispatch to isolated Hermes workers, then open it for review.

content.text: The PRD will recommend keeping Socket Mode initially and adapting dispatch behind it. The existing notes propose experimental relay mode; I’ll keep that as an alternative and make the runs API choice explicit, since neither path has passed Clanker’s hosted acceptance checks.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch *** Add File: /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/SLACK_GATEWAY_PRD.md +# Clanker Slack gateway PRD + +**Status: Draft for user review. No implementation or provisioning authorized by this document.** +**Date:** 2026-10-04 +**Product contract:** One shared Slack gateway routes authorized tasks to isolated Hermes runtimes. The user experience determines the integration; adapt Hermes where necessary. + +## 1. Review decisions + +1. **Initial transport and host:** retain Socket Mode in one persistent Python gateway container on Cloudflare, provisionally. HTTP Events API on Workers remains an alternative, not a requirement for dynamic worker dispatch. +2. **Worker integration:** prefer Hermes's existing asynchronous runs API behind a trusted worker wrapper. Adapt the shared gateway's dispatch lifecycle rather than assuming the stock Slack adapter can dispatch dynamically unchanged. Experimental relay remains an alternative if the runs API cannot support the required controls. +3. **Initial Slack surfaces:** 1:1 DMs and explicitly admitted channels/threads; channel tasks require a bot mention. Reject MPIMs, Slack Connect/external senders and unknown audiences in v1. Preserve threaded replies, progress, clarification, approval and cancellation; broad native command parity is not required. +4. **Capacity policy:** bounded configurable workers, fair queuing between contexts, one active run per profile, and sequential ordinary turns within a profile. Queue later turns; owner-authorized cancel/control messages can act on the current task. +5. **Provisioning:** Cloudflare is preferred, but paid capability, budget, instance suitability and persistence behavior must be confirmed before deployment. This draft does not approve spending. + +These are proposals for review. Existing `MOD_HERMES.md` proposes relay; this draft offers runs API as the initial candidate and does not silently amend that document. + +## 2. Problem and intended experience + +The stock Slack listener and reply code can be useful, but Clanker requires a task to outlive the gateway's current agent invocation and any assigned worker. Receiving ten task events from ten different authorized users must create ten owner/context-scoped tasks. Capacity may run only some immediately; the remainder wait fairly. None share a private Hermes agent, profile mount, browser state or task authority. + +The gateway is one trusted service. Multiple replicas, maximum throughput discovery and load benchmarking are not v1 prerequisites. One service may include transport and trusted control components; it must not execute arbitrary agent code. + +### Concrete journeys + +| Journey | Required user-visible behavior | +| --- | --- | +| Private browser task | User DMs a request, sees accepted/queued status, receives useful progress and a verified result in that DM. The assigned worker loads only their authorized context. | +| Ten independent users | Ten DM requests become ten distinct tasks tied to the right owners. With a smaller pool, queued users retain their place and eventually receive their own results. | +| Shared collaboration | Two admitted participants contribute to one channel thread. They share its authorized conversation context, without loading either participant's private account state. | +| Private access during shared work | Shared work identifies a need for Alice's private account. The gateway obtains Alice's authorization privately and creates/links a private task. Private observations return to Alice; sharing selected content requires her exact approval. | +| Human input and recovery | A task waits for clarification or a private access form. The worker can be released after a durable checkpoint. Valid input resumes the same task once, even if the prior worker was replaced. | + +## 3. Responsibilities and boundaries + +| Component | Owns | Does not own | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Shared gateway | Slack connection, admission, authenticated identity, audience mapping, durable task acceptance, safe progress/replies, owner-bound controls | Browser execution, deciding capacity, decrypting vault secrets in chat, arbitrary agent code | +| Scheduler/pool manager | Fair dispatch, profile lease, worker assignment, capacity bounds, clean-worker lifecycle, recovery coordination | Deriving human identity from model text, Slack publication authority | +| Isolated worker | Hermes, Browser Use driver, local Chromium, scoped profile/files, run events and checkpoints | Broad Slack/cloud credentials, other profiles, independent destination selection | +| Durable context store | Versioned authorized history/browser/files and checkpoints beyond worker lifetime | Treating object keys supplied by agents as access grants | +| Trusted vault/access service | Slack OIDC, owner/task/site authorization, secure submission, protected storage, durable access-ready signal | Sending passwords/setup keys through Slack, model inputs or queues | + +The gateway submits an authorized task to the scheduler. The scheduler selects a worker and supplies a scoped assignment. The gateway never assumes an event maps to a permanently allocated user VM. Storage and vault implementation are separate component decisions; this PRD defines their contracts. + +```mermaid +flowchart LR + Slack[Slack] <--> G[One trusted gateway] + G --> T[Durable task and delivery records] + T --> Q[Queue and scheduler] + Q --> W[Assigned isolated worker
Hermes + Browser Use + Chromium] + W <--> S[Authorized durable context] + W --> R[Bound run events and results] + R --> G + G <--> V[Trusted access and approval flows] + V --> T +``` + +## 4. Identity and routing requirements + +**G1. Authenticated identity.** Derive installation/workspace and sender from the authenticated Slack transport. Socket Mode uses its authenticated connection; HTTP, if selected, verifies the signature against raw bytes and rejects stale requests. Reject unknown installations/workspaces and senders. Model prose, submitted profile names, display names and email addresses confer no authority. + +**G2. Context selection.** Map a 1:1 DM to an owner-private profile. Map a channel/thread to a profile belonging to its admitted audience, with a thread-specific conversation session. Distinct audiences must not share private memory or browser state. Include tenant identity in every mapping. Fail closed on missing routes; never use a privileged default profile. + +**G3. Audience admission.** Confirm the channel is admitted and distinguish 1:1 IM from multi-person DM before context selection. Reject unsupported surfaces with a fixed safe response where appropriate. Workspace membership alone does not grant private-channel or personal-context access. Revalidate the permitted destination before delivery; membership/authorization changes suspend affected work for reconciliation. + +**G4. Distinct authorities.** Track requester, resource owner and output audience separately. Another participant can contribute to shared work without controlling a linked private task, approving an account action, reading private results or cancelling another owner's private run. + +**G5. Worker confinement.** Mount/load exactly the assigned context and its permitted files/browser state. Agent execution receives neither gateway/platform administrator credentials nor arbitrary storage access. Profile configuration is useful routing machinery, not the security boundary; the prior cross-profile session-search finding remains a release constraint. + +## 5. Trusted envelopes + +These are required semantics, not a frozen wire schema. Trusted components construct and validate identity and routing fields; worker output cannot change them. + +| Envelope | Required semantics | +| --- | --- | +| Accepted event | Schema version, authenticated installation/tenant/workspace, sender, surface classification, channel/thread/message IDs, transport event identity, semantic duplicate identity, received time and normalized intent/input or scoped attachment references | +| Task | Stable task ID, event association, requester, owner when applicable, authorized context/profile and conversation session, fixed permitted destination/audience, task kind, state/version, parent/private-task association when relevant, checkpoint reference and approved access handles | +| Assignment | Task ID, run/attempt ID, context ID, lease and fencing generation, worker identity, scoped state references/version, bounded execution policy and authenticated callback/control capability | +| Worker event/result | Task/run/attempt IDs, assigned worker and fencing generation, monotonic event sequence, event kind, safe progress/result or scoped artifact/checkpoint references, verified outcome evidence and failure/uncertainty classification | +| Approval/input | Opaque request ID, task/run association, intended owner, exact action or input purpose, immutable content/action digest, audience where sharing is requested, expiry and single-use decision state | + +Accept callbacks only from the assigned authenticated worker and current generation. Reject stale/wrong-task output. Treat worker event text as untrusted content and apply disclosure rules before Slack delivery. Do not place credentials, broad bearer tokens or secrets in task messages or logs. + +## 6. Acceptance, deduplication and ordering + +**G6. Durable acceptance before success.** Persist the accepted event and task/dispatch intent before acknowledging a task event. If persistence fails, do not claim acceptance. Keep transport acknowledgement within Slack's three-second budget; worker startup and model calls occur later. Unsupported/no-op events may be acknowledged without creating tasks. + +**G7. Two levels of deduplication.** Repeated transport delivery resolves to the original acceptance record. Also merge Slack `message` and `app_mention` notifications for the same underlying message. Do not collapse an intentional edit or separate user message. Use transport-specific interaction/command identities and make control consumption idempotent. Deduplication must survive gateway restart; the stock in-memory TTL cache is insufficient. + +**G8. Recoverable dispatch.** Persist acceptance and an outbox/dispatch intent together or use an equivalent recoverable transition. Queue publication failure leaves a retryable accepted task. Queue redelivery does not launch another active attempt. A duplicate event receives success once its original durable acceptance is known. + +**G9. Profile serialization.** Scheduler leases permit one active run per profile, including shared profiles with multiple thread sessions. Preserve accepted turn order within that profile. Fairly service independent contexts under configured capacity; a busy user cannot monopolize all slots. Throughput ceilings and multi-gateway routing are deferred. + +## 7. Progress, replies and controls + +**G10. Delivery association.** Every progress, clarification, artifact and completion belongs to a task/run and server-selected destination. Socket Mode is inbound transport; replies still use Slack APIs. Workers return events/results to the gateway rather than directly posting to Slack. + +**G11. Durable delivery.** Record delivery intent and outcome separately from execution. Retry rate-limited/transient Slack failures with bounded backoff and respect Slack retry guidance. Restarting the gateway must not launch the browser task merely because its reply was undelivered. Reconcile ambiguous sends where possible; retain unresolved delivery status rather than claiming exactly-once Slack publication. + +**G12. Useful status.** Show accepted/queued state, meaningful progress, waiting reason, completion, cancellation or actionable failure. Coalesce repetitive progress. Do not claim an account action succeeded from a generated answer alone; completion requires worker outcome evidence or an explicit uncertain result. + +**G13. Owner-bound approval.** Validate authenticated clicker against the durable approval owner and current task/run. Bind consequential execution approval to the exact action; changed details require a new request. Private-result sharing approval additionally binds exact content/artifacts and destination audience. Tool permission approval alone is not publication consent. Enforce expiry and single consumption; denied, foreign and replayed decisions cannot resume execution. + +**G14. Cancellation.** An authorized owner may cancel their private task; shared task controls follow an explicit requester/owner policy, proposed as task requester only for v1. Queued cancellation prevents dispatch. Running cancellation reaches the assigned run and revokes further execution authority. Report `cancelling` until stop is observed, and disclose any external action already performed or whose outcome is uncertain. Late callbacks cannot revive a cancelled task. + +## 8. Human input, persistence and recovery + +**G15. Waiting input.** Persist request purpose, owner, task and expiry outside the worker. Clarification text can use its admitted Slack surface; account secrets use the separate secure access flow. An access-ready signal carries a safe handle, never a password. Atomically consume valid input and record readiness once. Reject mismatched/expired/replayed input; input arriving after cancellation does not resume work. + +**G16. Worker release.** A waiting worker may be released only after a durable task/checkpoint transition. Run and approval state held only in process memory cannot justify scale-down. Resuming on another worker re-establishes the pending intent from persisted state; do not assume an old in-memory approval resolver survives replacement. + +**G17. Context persistence.** At task start, load the authorized durable context version. Checkpoint history, browser state and files consistently at defined safe points and before clean release. Use lease/fencing validation for checkpoint publication. Close/flush SQLite and browser state, or use a supported consistent snapshot; copying live files is not established as safe. Never reuse a dirty private worker for another context without verified reset/replacement. + +**G18. Failure classification.** Track accepted, queued, preparing, running, waiting-for-input/approval, cancelling, completed, failed, cancelled and needs-reconciliation states, with durable transition versions. A worker outage makes the current attempt interrupted. Requeue only after reconciling its lease, checkpoint and possible external effects. Uncertain purchase/post/delete outcomes require verification or owner input, not blind replay. A stored browser session is not a restored live page or unfinished action. + +## 9. Hermes reuse and modification boundary + +Source findings refer to Hermes 0.21.5, tag `v2026.9.24`, commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`. Paths are under `.local/hermes-lab/upstream/`; these findings do not establish a deployed pass. + +| Source-verified capability/gap | Intended treatment | +| --- | --- | +| Slack `connect()` starts Bolt Socket Mode; registered listeners cover messages, mentions, commands and actions (`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:1601,1771`). | Reuse listener/reply functionality where it fits. Keep it in a normal Python runtime. Adapt dispatch and trusted controls; transport need not change. | +| Message builder derives sender/team/session source, with known MPIM and route pitfalls (Slack audit). | Reuse normalization selectively, enforce G1–G5 before hydration/dispatch. Do not trust stock private/shared classification unchanged. | +| Simple proxy mode posts text/history to `/v1/chat/completions` and consumes text SSE (`gateway/run_turn.py:2744`). | It proves remote invocation exists, but does not implement dynamic pool assignment, task persistence or owner-bound controls. Do not declare the architecture solved by configuring it. | +| Runs API supports asynchronous admission, status/events, approval, steer/stop and durable idempotency (`gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py:186`). | Candidate worker boundary. Use per-context authenticated scopes, stable idempotency/session IDs and a trusted wrapper enforcing task/lease association. Verify available capabilities against the pinned worker. | +| Run ownership is checked by authenticated API scope; exact approval request IDs are supported (`api_server_runs.py:977,1072`). | Map Slack identity/owner to task authority in the trusted gateway. API scope is not automatically a Slack owner. | +| Stock Slack duplicate cache is process memory; approval buttons gate on bot admission (Slack audit; `gateway/platforms/helpers.py:20`). | Add durable deduplication and owner-bound approvals. Reuse display components only after control semantics are adapted. | +| Experimental RelayAdapter exchanges normalized events/actions with an external connector. Referenced connector repository was not publicly resolvable. | Alternative extension seam if runs integration fails a required journey. No requirement to rewrite the complete connector or adopt relay before testing the smaller candidate. | + +The shared gateway needs an adapted task lifecycle: normalize/admit → persist task → scheduler dispatch → bound worker events → durable delivery. Stock adapter use unchanged is not sufficient for that lifecycle. The precise patch/plugin boundary follows focused source validation during implementation, after PRD approval. + +## 10. Provisional Cloudflare mapping + +| Responsibility | Initial candidate | Caveat | +| --- | --- | --- | +| One persistent Slack transport | Cloudflare Container running adapted Python Slack gateway, Socket Mode | Paid capability and reliable persistent-connection lifecycle unverified; Slack transport reconnects must preserve durable task state. | +| Trusted task/control APIs and access UI | Workers | Keep arbitrary Hermes/browser execution outside Workers. Access/vault internals are separate scope. | +| Dispatch and coordination | Queues plus Durable Object scheduler/profile leases and durable structured records | Queue delivery is at least once; scheduling, ordering and fencing are application responsibilities. Choose an authoritative record store explicitly. | +| Isolated task runtime | Assigned Cloudflare Container, subject to proving required execution isolation | Validate that the offered isolation meets the selected worker boundary; do not call every container a verified VM sandbox. | +| Durable scoped profile/browser/files | R2 with versioned manifests/checkpoints, provisionally | Object storage is not a live POSIX/SQLite/browser-profile mount. Restore/checkpoint integration and crash consistency require proof. | + +**Rationale:** retaining Socket Mode preserves existing adapter behavior and avoids making an HTTP rewrite the first prerequisite. Dynamic authorized dispatch is the actual change. A persistent gateway is acceptable for v1. If container availability/cost or the reuse experiment defeats this approach, switch to HTTP ingress on Workers and retain the same task contracts. Slack HTTP ingress requires signature validation and three-second acknowledgement independently of backend startup. + +Costs include paid container running resources, Workers/Durable Objects, storage/queue usage and worker capacity. No cost total is asserted without account capability and workload checks. Do not provision a paid plan from approval of this document alone. + +## 11. Minimal v1 acceptance + +All scenarios below are **pending**. Record pinned versions, real versus synthetic environment, observed task/context/run IDs, assertions, failure evidence and limitations. Reuse the evidence ledger in `VERIFICATION_STRATEGY.md`. + +| Check | Required evidence | Environment | +| --- | --- | --- | +| A1: Ten distinct owners | Ten authenticated input events produce ten distinct owner/context-scoped tasks; bounded pool dispatches fairly; each result maps correctly; no concurrent runs for one profile. This is a correctness scenario, not a throughput benchmark. | Synthetic transport/worker test initially; label it synthetic. Real two-user checks below remain required. | +| A2: Real private/shared routing | Two real Slack users complete concurrent DMs and contribute in a shared thread. Verify histories/destinations and rejection of foreign tenant, unknown route and unsupported MPIM without private worker dispatch. | Real Slack for normal paths; synthetic identities for unavailable tenant/surface negatives. | +| A3: Duplicate and restart acceptance | Replay a task envelope and message/mention pair; crash between acceptance/queue publish; restart gateway. One accepted task remains recoverably dispatchable without duplicate active execution. | Controlled failure injection with synthetic transport; real Slack delivery smoke. | +| A4: Owner controls and sharing | B cannot approve/cancel A's private work. Owner's expired/replayed/changed-action decision is rejected. A privately reviews exact result content and explicitly approves its shared destination before publication. | Synthetic negative tests plus real two-user Slack interaction journey. | +| A5: Access resume and worker replacement | Wait for secure input, checkpoint/release worker, save authorized dummy access, resume the original task once on a replacement worker with scoped history/browser/files. Late input cannot revive cancellation. | Real Slack/access UI and isolated browser workers, dummy account data. | +| A6: Delivery and uncertain actions | Worker completion followed by Slack failure/restart retries delivery without rerunning the task. A lost external-action response enters reconciliation and does not automatically replay the action. Cancellation rejects late output. | Controlled failure injection; real Slack/browser confirmation where applicable. | +| A7: Runtime boundary | Agent code cannot read another owner's profile/browser/files, broad Slack/cloud credentials or trusted vault keys. Retest the cross-profile recall reproduction within the chosen execution boundary. | Actual deployed worker runtime with dummy secrets and adversarial probes. | + +Passing mocked source tests or one owner's tool-free Slack inference does not satisfy these journeys. No maximum-load experiment, multiple gateway replicas or full public SaaS onboarding is required to accept v1. + +## 12. Scope limits and implementation entry + +This PRD covers the gateway experience and integration boundaries. It does not select the model funding arrangement, implement the vault, settle manual versus automatic TOTP, define the full VM/provider isolation design, add billing/onboarding, or require deferred operator/provider privacy controls. Those decisions remain in their own component scope. + +After user review, first prove one accepted DM can be durably dispatched through the candidate worker API and returned to its original destination, including a denied foreign approval and one restart. Then extend to the remaining acceptance journeys. Patch Hermes or introduce custom connector code only for demonstrated contract gaps. + +**Current blocker:** implementation awaits user review; there is no blocker to reviewing this draft. Cloudflare paid capability, worker boundary/persistence proof and the final adapter/API seam are prerequisites to deployment, not prerequisites to drafting the contract. + +## References + +- [V1 scope](V1_SCOPE.md), [verification strategy](VERIFICATION_STRATEGY.md), [existing Hermes change proposals](MOD_HERMES.md). +- [Pinned baseline](verification/hermes/baseline.json), [Slack source audit and probes](verification/audit-slack-notes.md), [isolation audit](verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md). +- [Pinned Slack adapter](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py), [pinned runs API](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py), [pinned relay contract](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/website/docs/developer-guide/relay-connector-contract.md). +- [Slack Socket Mode](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/using-socket-mode/), [HTTP Events API](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/), [request verification](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/verifying-requests-from-slack/), [interactions](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/). +- [Cloudflare Containers lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/concepts/architecture/), [Containers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), [Queues guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/), [Queues external consumers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/). *** End Patch"));
